evidence: src/application/usecases/CreateTaskUseCase.ts: private generateId() returns `task_${Date.now()}_${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2)}`, the same rule copied
src/application/usecases/AssignTaskUseCase.ts: execute() builds `new Task(task.id, task.projectId, task.title, task.description, task.status, task.dueDate, userId)` instead of using entity behaviour
src/application/usecases/MarkTaskAsDoneUseCase.ts: execute() calls `task.markAsDone()`, changing state through entity behaviour, which conflicts with AssignTaskUseCase
src/application/usecases/CreateTaskUseCase.ts: hard-codes starting state `'todo'` and assignee `null` in the Task constructor call
src/application/usecases/ListTasksUseCase.ts: has executeByStatus/executeByAssignee/executeAll instead of the module's single execute() convention
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
All five files serve one cohesive concern: application use cases for projects and tasks. They fail the rubric in two ways.

1. A rule is duplicated. The ID-generation rule (a prefix, then Date.now(), then a random base-36 suffix) appears twice, as a private generateId() in CreateProjectUseCase and again in CreateTaskUseCase. This rule should live in one place, such as an injected IdGenerator.

2. The module handles Task state changes inconsistently. MarkTaskAsDoneUseCase changes a task through the entity's own behaviour (task.markAsDone()). AssignTaskUseCase skips the entity and rebuilds a whole new Task through its 7-argument constructor, copying every field and swapping in assigneeId. That puts assignment logic in the application layer, where any invariants Task enforces are skipped.

There are also smaller problems:
- CreateTaskUseCase hard-codes the new task's starting state ('todo' status, null assignee) instead of getting it from a domain factory.
- The 'Task not found' lookup-and-throw guard is repeated in AssignTaskUseCase and MarkTaskAsDoneUseCase.
- ListTasksUseCase has three methods (executeByStatus, executeByAssignee, executeAll), unlike the single execute() used by the other files.
